name: Alok Industries Limited
tagline: Reliance/JM Financial ARC-controlled vertically integrated textile major, still carrying a deeply negative consolidated net worth of ~-Rs 21,528 Cr as of March 2026 (worse than the prior year) and near-zero-to-negative ROCE, seven years after its 2019-20 IBC resolution. business_overview: Alok Industries manufactures cotton and polyester yarn, fabrics, garments and home textiles. It emerged from Corporate Insolvency Resolution Process in 2019-20 under a resolution plan giving Reliance Industries (RIL) 40.01% and JM Financial Asset Reconstruction Company 34.99% of equity, with ~Rs 17,384 Cr of the restructured debt interest-free for the first eight years. Despite that concessional structure, the balance sheet remains deeply impaired.

fundamentals_narrative: Alok Industries remains, seven years post-resolution, one of India's rare IBC cases where the resolved entity's net worth is still deeply negative and getting worse (-Rs 21,528 Cr at Mar 2026 vs -Rs 20,630 Cr a year prior), with Rs 24,993 Cr of accumulated losses. RIL's own attributable share of that negative net worth is ~-Rs 8,613 Cr. The interest-free debt cushion for the first eight years has bought time, not a turnaround: ROCE is negative, revenue is flat-to-declining over five years, and quarterly losses (Rs 138-193 Cr range through FY26) continue even as they narrow slightly. RIL is reportedly deconsolidating the unit, which if anything signals reduced strategic commitment rather than an inflection.
